issues.claim: Four family outcomes the third pass wrote are run by no bar. A build of the old text gives way, refuses or moves further than the laws, and keeps law 1 (item (a)'s chain in a zone excepted, which §5.3's row catches). (a) §4.8 The harbour mouth (l. 8401; P4) lays the chain 'at the nearest heads or shore points along the entrance whose gate and towers §2.7's laws admit, else not laid', and the fixed-place sentence (l. 3254-3256) has it wait at an epoch. No bar puts a raised way's zone over a harbour mouth at generation, and T110-4 (a)'s T-V6-48 variant (l. 19636-19638) runs only §5.3's row. (b) §7.1 Raised ways (l. 11145-11150; D3) and V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.wall` keep-clear form (V09 l. 2102; V9-2) bend a raised or aqueduct stroke that would end under a wall's band or wall strips or run along within them. No bar runs such a stroke: T110-2 (1)'s hand aqueducts (l. 19315-19324) and T-V9-52 do not. (c) §4.8's S7 lead (l. 8344; P9) admits a tower in an over crossing's strip margin under no span, where the old words moved it clear. T110-2 (1)'s tower clause (l. 19300-19302) runs only a tower 'under it'. (d) S5a's pin rule (l. 6600; P2) runs on the epoch path ('an epoch circuit', l. 3146), but every barred-pin run is at generation or a regeneration (T110-2 (3), (6)). J146 and J151 grade such gaps minor.

issues.claim: Four bar texts still restate law 1 (4) or (5) in their own words, against adjudication-r7x's form F5 and R7-01 (2)'s sweep. Each names a place the laws do not give; S0 makes each bar assert the laws' outcome, so the grade is minor. (a) T110-2 (3) (l. 19366-19367; this pass's S9 (c)): 'no raised way's ends under the band, its wall strips or the channel'. Law 1 (4) binds a wall's line, band and wall strips, never its moat, which lies 'outside the outer half-band and a berm' (§4.4 Outer moats, l. 6638), so with the pin at the first point beyond the foot it may lie over an end's widened margin; the way-and-channel table's row (e) gives the moat its outcome. (b) T110-2 (3) (l. 19390-19391): 'the second castle's town-side gate fixed on its next side clear of that strip'. S3 (8) admits the side 'whose gate … lies where law 1 (5) and (6) admit it', the margin of an over crossing among them. (c) T-V6-47 (V06 l. 4219), twice: 'no gate, postern or tower in the under-deck strip but in an over crossing whose spans clear it' and the matching bar omit law 1 (5)'s 'never on a support's ring'. (d) T-V9-52 (V09 l. 4428): a slid gate 'moves back along the trace to the strip's edge its grip came from (a placed one to the nearer edge)', and 'a wall drawn along beneath the viaduct moves to the strip's edge'. Read on the under-deck strip, each place puts half a footprint or half a band in the strip, where row W13 and *Strips, zones and nearest points* give 'the first point at which these laws admit its footprint' and law 1 (4) with law 3 (END-L3) a line leaving on its entry side, its band outside. V09's repair seat listed (d) for this check. T110-2 (4)'s sibling (l. 19463-19464) states the band's place and agrees with the laws.

issues.claim: Row W12·C8 (ARCHITECTURE l. 3349) gives both locked sides of a landfall over a run beneath a deck: 'a locked raised way's spans and supports kept and the run beneath `breached`, a locked run kept and the spans and supports over it `ruined`'. It names T-V5-14 for both. T-V5-14's raised-way clause (V05 l. 2577-2579) runs only the first ('With the aqueduct locked, it is kept … and the run beneath is `breached` all the same'); its general 'a locked wall kept' (V05 l. 2537) is on a fixture with no raised way. A build that also spares the raised way's spans and supports over a locked run keeps law 1 and passes every bar. Under R7-01's grading, a cell whose named test does not hold its case is a minor.

issues.claim: T110-2 (3)'s third run (l. 19372-19375), the bar for P2's step (b), asserts the arterial 're-routed … through a lawful gate of the stage'. Three texts this pass wrote name that gate differently. §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 6600; P2) says '(b) else its arterial re-routed as law 2 (b) moves a ground way, to cross the boundary at a gate those laws admit (a gate S5b spawned among them; …)'. §4.4 S5b (l. 6650; P8) says 'its way else re-routed through a gate this step spawns', and the way-and-channel table's row (d) (l. 2916; M10) says 'else its way re-routed through a gate S5b spawns (law 2 (b))'. Law 2 (b) re-routes by the router that laid the way, between its nearest unmoved nodes, with no restriction on the gate. When N_k > c, routing through any lawful gate and routing through spawned gates alone both keep law 1 and N_k and pass the bar: a valid choice (J151). When N_k ≤ c, S5b 'spawns none' (l. 6653), so S5b's words leave the arterial no gate, and P2's 'among them' gives the outcome, a stage gate it may pass. A reading that let S5b's words bind P2 would take F-WALL's rung where law 2 (b) lays a lawful walled shape (PRB7H-GEN-04 (i)), and would be major; P2's own words exclude it. Each text restates law 2 (b) more narrowly than the laws, the class adjudication-r7x's root-cause ruling closes.
